subject: physics_2
question_text: What is the average wavelength of X-rays?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Hand-checked: the book (p.41) gives the X-ray wavelength range 10⁻⁸ m to 10⁻¹³ m and answers 10⁻¹⁰ m — that is the mid-point of the range taken on powers of ten (the geometric mid-point of the printed range), not the arithmetic mean; the arithmetic mean of 10⁻⁸ m and 10⁻¹³ m would be near 5 × 10⁻⁹ m.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The range of X-ray wavelengths
lines: The wavelength range of X-rays is
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write both limits with their powers of ten and the unit m.
steps.why: The average only means something once the range is on paper, so the range line earns its own mark.
common_mistakes: Writing the limits without units. Both limits are lengths in metres: 10⁻⁸ m and 10⁻¹³ m.
Quoting the visible-light range. X-rays are far shorter: 10⁻⁸ m down to 10⁻¹³ m.

recall.must_convey: That X-ray wavelengths run from 10⁻⁸ m down to 10⁻¹³ m.
accept: ten to the minus eight to ten to the minus thirteen

steps.memory_tip: Two limits, five powers of ten apart: 10⁻⁸ m and 10⁻¹³ m.

steps.label: The average wavelength
lines: The value usually quoted as the average
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The average is taken on the powers of ten, not by adding the two limits.
steps.why: 10⁻¹⁰ m is the conventional typical X-ray wavelength (1 Å, about one atomic diameter), and it is the value the book marks. It is NOT an average of the two printed limits by any rule: the arithmetic mean of 10⁻⁸ m and 10⁻¹³ m is about 5 × 10⁻⁹ m, and the geometric mean is 10⁻¹⁰·⁵ ≈ 3 × 10⁻¹¹ m. Quote the standard value rather than trying to compute one from the range.
common_mistakes: Averaging the two limits arithmetically and writing about 5 × 10⁻⁹ m.
Taking the geometric mean of the limits and writing about 3 × 10⁻¹¹ m — that is a real mid-point of the range, but it is not the value asked for.

recall.must_convey: That the average wavelength of X-rays is about 10⁻¹⁰ m.
accept: ten to the minus ten metres
average is ten power minus ten
reject: five into ten to the minus nine

steps.memory_tip: 10⁻¹⁰ m is one angstrom — atom-sized, which is why X-rays can probe crystals.

insider_note: Both powers of ten carry marks: the range 10⁻⁸ m to 10⁻¹³ m earns the first, and 10⁻¹⁰ m as the average earns the second.
